episodes.193817: A line of thunderstorms moving northeast out of Colorado into south-central Wyoming resulted in wind gusts exceeding 60 mph along portions of Interstate 80 on the evening of the 25th.
episodes.194021: A plume of monsoonal moisture flowed northward into New Mexico on August 26th, providing ample fuel for afternoon showers and storms to develop along the Sacramento Mountains and Ruidoso. Storms producing locally heavy rainfall developed and moved over the recent burn scars in and around Ruidoso, producing burn scar flash flooding along the Rio Ruidoso and portions of the South Fork burn scar.||Key Impacts: burn scar flash flooding.
episodes.194040: A cold pool aloft and surface front caused a round of strong to severe storms over all of southern New England. Hail from 1 to 2 inches fell in MA, RI, and CT while localized flash flooding was observed in southern RI and MA.

episodes.194505: Numerous thunderstorms developed across the area resulting in wind gusts of 60-66 mph. Wind damage was also reported in eastern Gove county near Quinter.
episodes.194713: A meandering front, very high moisture and diurnal heating combined with sea breezes triggered locally heavy rainfall across inland areas. Very weak storm motion produced slow moving, heavy rainfall producing storms.
episodes.194715: A meandering front, very high moisture and diurnal heating combined with sea breezes triggered locally heavy rainfall across inland areas. Very weak storm motion produced slow moving, heavy rainfall producing storms.
episodes.194822: A line of severe thunderstorms developed as they moved into southwest South Dakota. These storms produced wind gusts to over 70 mph, along with embedded areas of hail, as they tracked through southwest and south-central South Dakota.
episodes.194856: A thunderstorm became severe over western portions of Weston County, producing wind gusts to near 70 mph west of Upton.
episodes.194857: A thunderstorm became severe over south-central Weston County and tracked northeast into the Newcastle area. The storm produced wind gusts to around 60 mph.
episodes.194858: A thunderstorm briefly became severe over western Crook County, producing gusty winds near Pine Haven.
episodes.194859: Large hail and strong wind gusts accompanied a severe thunderstorm southeast of Sundance.
episodes.195122: The thermal cap diurnally weakened along a weak surface trough from north central Nebraska into central South Dakota by very late afternoon, which allowed an isolated strong to severe thunderstorm to develop. The storm tracked slowly eastward through the early evening. Very large hail occurred early in the life cycle, with a transition toward damaging wind and torrential rainfall as it shifted east of the Missouri River.
episodes.195155: A complex of thunderstorms developed during the afternoon of August 26, and grew upscale into a line of storms that produced widespread wind damage across central and eastern Minnesota. There were likely hundreds, if not thousands of trees damaged across the Twin Cities metro area.
episodes.195370: A few thunderstorms affected the tidal Potomac River with gale-force wind gusts during the mid to late afternoon hours.
episodes.195388: An isolated severe thunderstorm produced localized wind damage in the Fredericksburg area.
episodes.195435: Weak thunderstorms produced some strong outflow winds in excess of 60 mph. Several trees were knocked down in the town of Conde, one of which fell on a residence.
episodes.195511: For the end of August, ridging was noted across the eastern two-thirds of the CONUS. This upper-level pattern and associated surface high pressure system brought afternoon highs in the upper 90s and low 100s in addition to dew points in the 70s and lower 80s to much of eastern Nebraska and western Iowa. As a result, excessive heat was experienced by many the afternoons of both the 25th and the 26th, where heat indices ranged from 110 to 125 degrees during peak heating in the afternoon. |By the 26th, a shortwave trough ejected into the Pacific Northwest and moved across the northern Rockies. Isolated supercells developed the afternoon of the 26th along a weakening cold front that was slowly pushing south into northern Nebraska. While most of the severe weather from these storms remained north and west of the Omaha NWS County Warning Area, one supercell did make its way into portions of northeast Nebraska bringing hail up to 3.25 inches in diameter.|By the 29th, another shortwave trough ejected into the northern Plains immediately behind the disturbance that brought large hail to portions of northern Nebraska on the 26th. A surface low-pressure associated with this disturbance developed in south-central Canada, with a secondary low pressure that developed near the North Dakota-South Dakota border. A surface cold front was also noted as extending from northeast South Dakota into eastern Colorado. Scattered thunderstorms developed along and ahead of this front across much of eastern Nebraska and western Iowa during the early afternoon hours. While most of these thunderstorms remained under severe limits, there were a few instances of wind gusts ranging from 60 to 70 miles per hour, and one report of quarter sized hail from northeast Nebraska.
episodes.195630: A passing cold front and shortwave combined with a moisture moving in from around an upper level low to produce showers and thunderstorms, some with strong wind gusts. The storms mainly hit Fremont and Natrona Counties. One round of showers and storms hit around noon, with a wind gust of 58 mph reported along Hat Six Road to the East of Evansville. The second round of storms occurred in the evening hours, producing wind gusts over 58 mph from South Pass in the Wind River Mountains to the Casper Airport. Some notable wind gusts included 66 mph over South Pass and 63 mph at Natrona.
episodes.195631: A thunderstorm developed in the lee of the Wind River Mountains and become severe as it moved northeastward across Fremont County. The storm produced quarter size hail along Gas Hills Road to the east of Riverton and a 63 mph wind gust north of Shoshoni.
episodes.195647: Similar to August 24, environmental conditions were favorable for the development of waterspouts, landspouts, or tropical funnel clouds. A landspout was sighted in Donna during the afternoon of August 24th.
episodes.195745: A cold front propagated across our region, with the majority of the instability along the front. All threats were in play, but all of our reports were large hail.
episodes.195780: An upper-level disturbance generated isolated to scattered showers and thunderstorms throughout eastern New York on August 26, 2024. One thunderstorm became severe in the Upper-Hudson Valley where 1 inch hail was reported in Warren County.
episodes.195976: Showers and thunderstorms developed across the Panhandles during the afternoon and evening hours in relation to a surface boundary in the area. The combination of daytime heating, where afternoon highs were exceeding 100 degrees, sufficient wind shear and plenty of dry air supportive of microbursts, resulted in severe wind gusts across the region. Several microbursts occurred that resulted in winds of 60 to 80mph estimated have occurred. Because of this, wind damage occurred across portions of the central and northern Texas Panhandle.
episodes.196024: A lone supercell thunderstorm developed over eastern Brown county during the mid afternoon hours of August 26th. As this storm migrated slowly east, it grew upscale producing very large hail along a swath form south of Bassett to the O'Neill and Inman areas. Hail up to 4 inches in diameter was reported, along with numerous reports of 2 to 3 inch diameter hail.
episodes.196121: Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed over western Kansas. One storm moved into southern Barton County and increased in intensity. There was a report of a downed power line.
episodes.196143: Scattered storms developed across central Virginia on August 26 under a belt of northwest flow aloft. A few storms became severe and produced damaging winds across portions of central Virginia.
episodes.196218: A cold upper level low moved across New Hampshire on August 26th.  The colder temperatures lowered the freezing levels which allowed for abundant hail to fall out of developing thunderstorms during the afternoon hours.  This led to numerous reports of large damaging hail across New Hampshire.
episodes.196347: Afternoon thunderstorms associated with the sea breeze produce strong marine wind gusts in the Tampa Bay area.
